correctness.rationale: Exact subgroup-indicator identity yields multipliers q(t−1); the zero set is precisely the one-zero-block shell. Character orthogonality gives its exact inverse transform, and a one-sign-change binomial sum gives the sharp endpoint norm. The result holds for all m≥1 and is independently checked by full integer transforms at m=1,2; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The full-group range projection is a canonical stable-recovery operator. At the first singular member of a natural infinite graph family its sharp L1/L∞ norm is explicitly determined and grows (q/e)2^q, contrasting sharply with its least positive L2 singular value q. It is an exact natural invariant and structurally meaningful singularity threshold, not a routine arbitrary finite census.
